Combined upper and lower endoscopy report
Patient: Marisol Vandermeer (fictional)
Date of birth: 1957-04-03
Synthetic record: H2-SYN-1101
Procedure date: 2026-10-16
Endoscopist: Kwabena Thistlewood, MD, Gastroenterology (fictional)
Site of care: freestanding ambulatory surgical center, POS 24
Anesthesia: monitored anesthesia care by Annika Castellanos-Webb, CRNA (fictional), documented and billed by the anesthesia group
Indications
Iron deficiency anemia, with ferritin 5 ng/mL and hemoglobin 9.8 g/dL on 2026-09-24, and occasional epigastric burning. No visible bleeding and no diarrhea. She has never had an endoscopy of either kind.
Procedure summary
Examination | Instrument | Furthest point reached | Tissue sampled
Upper endoscopy (EGD) | Standard gastroscope | Third portion of the duodenum | Yes, duodenum and stomach
Colonoscopy | Adult colonoscope | Terminal ileum, about 6 cm beyond the ileocecal valve | No
Upper endoscopy
Consent was confirmed and the pre-procedure pause completed. Under direct vision the gastroscope crossed the upper esophageal sphincter and reached the third portion of the duodenum. Esophageal mucosa unremarkable; regular Z-line at 38 cm. On retroflexion the cardia and fundus looked normal. Patchy antral erythema, with no erosions or ulcers. Bulb, second portion and third portion of the duodenum unremarkable. For celiac disease I took four pieces from D2, the second portion of the duodenum, and two from the bulb with cold forceps, and for Helicobacter pylori three pieces from the antrum and incisura; each site went into its own container.
Colonoscopy
With the patient on her left side, the digital rectal examination showed nothing abnormal, and the adult colonoscope then passed easily around the colon. Cecal landmarks (appendiceal orifice, ileocecal valve) were documented with photographs. I entered the terminal ileum and inspected about 6 cm of it. Boston Bowel Preparation Scale score 8 (right 2, transverse 3, left 3). Scattered small-mouthed diverticula in the sigmoid colon. No polyps, masses, vascular lesions or blood; colonic and ileal mucosa normal. I deliberately did not take colon biopsies, because the mucosa was normal and she has no diarrhea. Retroflexion in the rectum showed small, non-bleeding internal hemorrhoids. Withdrawal time was 11 minutes.
Complications
None.
Impression
1. Antral erythema; duodenal and gastric biopsies taken.
2. Normal terminal ileum. Sigmoid diverticulosis and small internal hemorrhoids. No colonic source for the iron deficiency.
Plan
Await pathology and continue oral iron. If the biopsies do not explain the anemia, small bowel capsule endoscopy will be discussed at the follow-up visit.

The gastroscope was advanced through a normal esophagus into the stomach. A large amount of retained food and

Gastric outlet obstruction from an active pyloric channel ulcer, probably related to naproxen. Biopsies taken. The

Stop naproxen. High-dose proton pump inhibitor. Liquid diet. Await pathology.

Repeat upper endoscopy in about 8 weeks to check healing and, if the narrowing persists, to perform balloon dilation
and complete the examination of the duodenum.
